function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single individual—it emerged from the work of many thinkers and experimenters over millennia: | Era | Key figure(s) | Contribution | |-----|---------------|--------------| | **Ancient Greece** | *Thales of Miletus* (~600 BCE) | Noted static attraction when rubbing amber (“electrum”). | | **17th–18th Century** | *William Gilbert* (1544‑1603) – coined the term *electricus*, studied magnetism vs. electrostatics.
*Otto von Guericke* (1685) – experiments on Leyden jars. | Pioneered systematic study of electrical phenomena. | | **Late 1700s** | *Benjamin Franklin* (1706‑1790) – lightning rod, kite experiment, defined positive/negative charges.
*Alessandro Volta* (1745‑1827) – invented the voltaic pile (first battery). | Demonstrated practical sources of steady electric currents. | | **Early 1800s** | *Hans Christian Ørsted* (1777‑1851) – showed electromagnetism (current produces magnetic field).
*André-Marie Ampère* (1769‑1836) – formulated laws relating current and force. | Established foundational principles linking electricity and magnetism. | So while there isn’t a single “discoverer,” the cumulative discoveries—from ancient observations of static charge to modern electromagnetic theory—led us to understand and harness electricity today.
